name: Plus One
description: You are given a large integer represented as an integer array digits, where each digits[i] is the ith digit of the integer. Increment the large integer by one and return the resulting array of digits.
shortDescription: Increment a number represented as array by one

explanation.idea: Adding one is just schoolbook addition: start from the last digit, and carry only when a 9 rolls over to 0.
explanation.analogy: A car's odometer: 1299 → 1300. Only the trailing 9s roll over; once a digit doesn't overflow, nothing to its left changes.

computeIterative.summary: Walk from the right; the first digit below 9 just goes up and you stop.
steps: If it's less than 9, add one and return: no carry is needed.
If it's 9, it becomes 0 and the carry moves left.
If every digit was 9 (999), return a new array 1000: length n + 1 with a leading 1.
computeIterative.timeWhy: At most one pass, and usually it stops at the first digit.
computeIterative.spaceWhy: Works in place, except the all-9s case which needs a new array of n + 1.

computeWithArrayList.summary: General addition with a carry, building the result at the front of a list.
steps: Start with carry = 1 (the one being added).
From the right: sum = digit + carry, keep sum % 10, carry = sum / 10.
Insert each digit at the front of the list.
If a carry is left over, insert it at the front too, then copy to an array.
computeWithArrayList.timeWhy: list.add(0, x) shifts every element, so each insert is O(n). Appending and reversing would make it O(n).
computeWithArrayList.spaceWhy: The list and the result array.

computeWithRecursion.summary: The same carry, with recursion moving from the last index to the first.
steps: addOneRecursive(digits, index, carry) handles one digit and calls itself on index − 1.
At each digit: sum = digit + carry, store sum % 10, pass sum / 10 on.
When the index goes below 0, a remaining carry means a new leading 1.
computeWithRecursion.spaceWhy: Each call stays on the call stack until the first digit is done.

pitfalls: Converting the digits to an int or long overflows for long inputs (the input can have 100 digits).
Forgetting the all-9s case, which grows the array.
interview: Say the early-exit insight: once a digit isn't 9 you can return immediately.
Follow-up: add two digit arrays → same carry loop with two indices (see Add Binary, Add Two Numbers).
